stem:
Ishaan writes numbers with Roman landmarks: I $=1$, V $=5$, X $=10$, L $=50$. He wants to represent $39$.

Which plan follows landmark decomposition?

options.text: Answer "Roman numerals", naming the writing system instead of building $39$ from landmarks.
Place any mix of I, V, X, and L in any order until the symbols look long enough.
Take one XXX for $30$ (the largest useful landmark not past $39$), then IX for the remaining $9$.
Copy the digits $3$ and $9$ as drawn shapes and treat those shapes as the Roman form.

teacher.key_rationale: Largest useful landmark first: XXX for 30, then IX for 9. Naming the system swaps the task. Any-order symbols drop the largest-first rule. Copying printed digits captures surface shapes.
